context: A teacher walks a teen through research
purpose: Teach: 射程/救世主/宮廷/攻防/急落/惹き/激動/無念

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 桜さん、論文、歴史上の射程、本気で、扱っていましたね、絶対、本気で、立派、本当に、感心しました、絶対、本気で、本当に。
lines.en: Sakura, the scope and depth of your history paper were genuinely impressive. You took it seriously, and it really showed.
lines.style: Warm, measured approval. Eyes crinkling slightly. Genuine respect in the voice — no performance. A teacher noticing real work.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。当時、人々が、救世主のような、存在を、本気で、求めた歴史、論文で、論じました、絶対、本気で、深い、研究、できました、本当に、感謝。
lines.en: Thank you. I wrote about how people in that era desperately sought savior figures — it was something I really wanted to explore deeply.
lines.style: Quiet intensity. Direct eye contact. Not rehearsed — she's still thinking about the work. A slight lift at the end, genuine gratitude mixed with the weight of what she studied.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 平安時代の宮廷文化、本気で、論文で、扱っていましたね、絶対、桜さん、本気で、視野、広い、本当に、立派、本気で、絶対、感心。
lines.en: The way you handled Heian court culture was particularly thoughtful. You really broadened the lens on that period.
lines.style: Nodding slightly, reflective. Speaking a little slower, as if turning the idea over. Specific praise — not generic. The voice of someone who actually read it.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。歴史上、権力の攻防、本気で、複雑、扱いました、絶対、論文で、深い、研究、できました、本当に、感謝、しております、本気で、絶対。
lines.en: Yes. I tried to show how the power struggles of that time were so complicated — how they shaped everything. I'm grateful I could do that research.
lines.style: Steady, almost solemn. She's not performing earnestness — she's just speaking about something that mattered. A slight formality creeping in with gratitude, but still grounded.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 江戸末期、本気で、社会的地位の急落、論文で、扱っていましたね、絶対、本気で、現代にも、繋がる、本当に、立派、本気で、絶対、本気。
lines.en: And the Late Edo period section — the sudden shifts in social status — that connected so well to modern tensions. Really impressive work.
lines.style: Leaning in slightly, engaged. Voice has energy now, but measured. She's excited about the ideas, not the student. Speaking as a thinker to a thinker.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。歴史人物の魅力、本気で、人々を惹きつける、力、論文で、扱いました、絶対、本気で、深い、研究、できました、本当に、感謝、本気で。
lines.en: Thank you. I wanted to show how historical figures had this power to draw people in — what made them matter to people at the time. I think I found that through the research.
lines.style: Thoughtful pause before answering. Soft confidence underneath. She's not listing accomplishments — she's talking about discovery. Gratitude felt, not performed.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 明治の激動の時代、本気で、論文の重要な、テーマでしたね、絶対、桜さん、本気で、立派、本当に、感心しました、絶対、本気で、本当に、絶対。
lines.en: The Meiji period — all that upheaval — became such a crucial part of your argument. You handled it with real care.
lines.style: Slower pace. Gentle respect in the tone. Not just praise — recognition that she noticed how carefully Sakura treated difficult material. The warmth of a teacher who sees the student's effort.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。志半ば、無念に、亡くなった人物、論文で、扱いました、絶対、本気で、心、痛む、内容でした、本当に、絶対、本気で、感謝、本気、絶対、本当に。
lines.en: Yes. There were people in that period who died before they could finish what they started — with such regret. Writing about them was... it was hard, but important to me.
lines.style: Quieter now, more vulnerable. The pace drops. She's not just summarizing — she's admitting something. A slight break in the composure, then steadying. Genuine emotion under control.
